children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange remained under pressure Thursday morning despite the continued rise of crude oil prices.
Crude oil rose by nearly US$4 per barrel as tensions persist between the U.S. and Iran. Chicago soyoil also was higher while European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil were lower.
Statistics Canada reported on Wednesday 2025-26 canola ending stocks as of July 31 of 1.9 million tonnes, up by 19% compared with a year earlier and in line with the five-year average.

The majority of Saskatchewan and Alberta will receive precipitation Thursday with daytime temperatures failing to reach 20 degrees Celsius. However, southern Manitoba will see sunny skies and temperatures exceeding 25 C.
The Canadian dollar was down one-tenth of a U.S. cent compared with Wednesday's close.
Nearly 15,900 contracts were traded. Prices in Canadian dollars per metric ton as of 9:47 a.m. ET:
